# 07 Close the board: example, demo, glossary, ADR

## Outcome

An author can see flowchart styling working without reading a test, and ADR-0008 no longer
describes its amendment as future work.

## Why this ticket exists

The class-diagram and sequence boards both closed this way. Two documents currently say things this
board makes false, and one of them is an ADR — the repo's durable record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A flowchart example exercises every directive this board added: `style`, `classDef`, `class`,
      `A:::name`, `linkStyle` with an index, with a list, and `default`, plus `color` alongside a
      `fill`. Decide whether it extends `examples/complex-showcase.srn` or is a new file, and say
      why. It must produce **zero diagnostics**, not merely zero errors.
- [x] The `examples/` enumeration test covers it automatically — a new file needs no test wiring
      (board 2, `3589544`). Confirm rather than assume.
- [x] A demo page shows it. Check whether an existing flowchart demo should gain it rather than
      adding a page nobody links to.
- [x] **ADR-0008's amendment section is updated to record that it landed**, with the ADR's status
      handled the way this repo handles a superseded-in-part decision. Read the other ADRs first
      and follow whatever convention they show; if there is none, say so and propose one rather
      than inventing a mechanism silently.
- [x] `examples/class-full.srn`'s `%%` comment recommending translucent fills is revisited. It
      described a workaround for the gap ticket 06 closed. Keep the advice only if it is still the
      best guidance, and say which you decided.
- [x] `CONTEXT.md` records author styling as a term: the four flowchart directives, the two
      spellings of the apply-directive and that they mean one thing, that `linkStyle` addresses by
      index while everything downstream uses the edge id, and that `color` reaches label text.
      Mind the existing `_Avoid_:` lines — note that **Class** already warns about the CSS-class
      sense of the word "class".
- [x] **Found by ticket 01b.** `packages/core/src/parser/parseClassDiagram.ts:353-366` is badly
      stale: it claims style and interaction validation is "**not written yet**" and that
      `buildClassModel` "resolves `interactions` and `styles` to empty arrays, so today these
      statements parse and then vanish". All false — the gate has existed since ADR-0008 and now
      lives in `resolveStyles.ts`. A comment pointing at the wrong module for what ADR-0008 calls
      the security boundary is how a check ends up added in the wrong place. It wants a rewritten
      paragraph, not a word swap.
- [x] **Found by ticket 01b, with line numbers.** `docs/adr/0008-...md:16` still names
      `ResolvedClassStyle`, and `CONTEXT.md:238` defines "Author style" as class-diagram-only,
      reaching "a class's frame only, never its label text" — which tickets 03-06 falsify twice
      over.
- [x] **Added after 05c/05d.** `CONTEXT.md` records that a rendered SVG's internal ids are scoped
      per render (`__` + eight characters) and that markup is therefore **not byte-reproducible**
      across two renders of one document. That is consumer-visible: anyone diffing or snapshotting
      Siren output needs to know. The reasoning lives in `renderer/mintIdScope.ts`; the glossary
      needs the fact, not the argument.
- [x] **Added after 01b.** `docs/adr/0008-...md:16` still names `ResolvedClassStyle`, a type that no
      longer exists — ticket 01b renamed it to `ResolvedStyle`. Fix the reference. Do not rewrite
      the surrounding argument; only the name is stale.
- [x] `.dev/mermaid-diagram-roadmap.md` marks board 3 done and names what is next.
- [x] **Added after the compatibility measurement.** The roadmap points at
      `.dev/mermaid-compatibility-gaps.md` and states the position plainly: **a document that
      renders in Mermaid must render here, and that is an absolute condition.** The measured
      numbers (flowchart 5/39, classDiagram 12/13, sequenceDiagram 10/15) and the
      never-swallow-an-unimplemented-construct policy belong in front of whoever plans the next
      board, not buried in a scratch file they might not open. That file is
      gitignored, so the edit will not appear in `git status` — make it anyway.

- [x] **The planning lesson this board paid for three times.** Record in the board's `spec.md`,
      under a heading a future planner will actually read: **a ticket that changes a type must own
      every file that constructs OR asserts it.** Tickets 01, 03 and 06 each returned `blocked` for
      exactly this — 01 could not rename `classId` without `buildClassModel.test.ts`, 03 could not
      rename `classIds` without `parseClassDiagram.ts`, and 06 could not split `ResolvedStyle`
      without two test files holding 37 assertions. `tsc --noEmit` after a probe edit enumerates
      the set in seconds; guessing it does not. This costs one paragraph and would have saved three
      reissues.

## Status

Done (2026-09-06), commit f4b5186. 1 red-green slice plus documentation, with the non-behavioral
items declared as such and evidenced by grep and by executing the demo pages.

596 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean both, both packages build. All nine examples verified at zero
DIAGNOSTICS (not merely zero errors) by the integrator — which caught that `step-reveal.srn` was
tripping board 2's own connector-outlives-its-endpoint warning. Fixed in the same commit.

`render()` over the example files. The demo page is not unit-tested; verify it by loading or
executing it.
